extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy (especially philosophy of mathematics) and readers seeking an overview of Wittgenstein's later views on mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and evaluate later Wittgenstein's philosophy of mathematics: its method (therapeutic/descriptive), its diagnostics of errors (e.g., Platonism, mentalism), and its positive claims about rules, empirical regularities, and communal practices that underlie mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical identities are rules not propositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Arithmetical identities (such as ‘three times three is nine’) are not really propositions, as their superficial form indicates, but are certain kinds of rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret mathematical formulae as rules that license operations (e.g., replacement in extensional contexts) and govern practices rather than as descriptive statements about abstract entities. This reframing is central to resisting Platonist readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules are not arbitrary; grounded in empirical regularities
rubrics_metrics.description: These rules are not arbitrary; the rules in place are the only ones that could have been adopted because they are grounded in objectively verifiable empirical regularities (the empirical regularities are “hardened” into rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating whether a rule is legitimate, check whether it codifies robust behavioral or worldly regularities; lawful-seeming formal rules derive their non-arbitrary character from such antecedent regularities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement in action (consensus of doing) is constitutive of mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement within a community is a crucial presupposition of the very existence of mathematics – not agreement of opinion but a consensus of action or form of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish agreement-as-opinion from agreement-as-practice: mathematical correctness relies on shared trained reactions and practices (a consensus of doing), which must already obtain for mathematical norms to exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between applied and pure (not-yet-applied) mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: The distinction between applied and pure mathematics helps explain why mathematicians are attracted to Platonism: applied mathematics shows effectiveness, whereas unapplied formalism tempts 'prose' that reifies mathematics as discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In assessing claims about mathematical reality, consider whether appeal to applicability (or lack thereof) motivates metaphysical rhetoric; applied success grounds interest without committing to Platonist ontology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophical method should be therapeutic/descriptive, not foundational/explanatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy's role is therapeutic: to expose conceptual confusions and remind us where concepts are 'at home' rather than to defend grand foundations; philosophy should describe practices, producing perspicuous representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject attempts to give philosophical 'explanations' that import concepts from empirical science into mathematics; aim to dissolve pseudo-problems by showing illicit transfers of language and misuse of concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique of Platonism as illicit ‘transfer’ of empirical language
rubrics_metrics.description: Platonism mistakes mathematical formulae for propositions about abstract, mind-independent objects by transferring the language of 'reality' from empirical contexts to mathematics; this transfer generates pseudo-problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating Platonist claims, look for the transfer move (extending 'reality' talk into mathematical discourse) and show how it detaches concepts from their ordinary language-games, producing misleading philosophical puzzles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical objectivity explained by behavioral regularities, not metaphysics
rubrics_metrics.description: Wittgenstein accepts a form of objectivity but locates its source in contingent, robust behavioral regularities and shared practices rather than in transcendent mathematical entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for perceived objectivity of mathematics by documenting stable communal practices and training that produce reliable agreement, rather than positing a metaphysical realm of mathematical objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule-following paradox and the indispensability of training/practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Because 'any course of action can be made out to accord with the rule', no exhaustive list of directives can determine rule-following; successful rule-following depends on training and the brute fact of communal practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain mathematical competence by pointing to pedagogical processes, corrective interventions, and community standards that stabilize interpretations, rather than by supplying an exhaustive algorithm or inner guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardened/archived norms: conversion of empirical regularities into rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical regularities are 'hardened' or 'condensed' into rules and 'deposited in the archives'—an empirical pattern becomes a norm that governs judgment of right and wrong in mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace normative status to prior recurring practices: demonstrate how frequent, stable ways of doing are codified into formal rules and thus acquire a protected, archived status that resists casual tampering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between background contingency and system necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a difference between the contingent behavioral background (which makes mathematics possible) and the necessity internal to mathematical systems (relations between archived items); background is contingent, content is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing mathematical claims, separate the empirical conditions that enable the practice (contingent) from the normative / logical necessities that operate inside the archived system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics is non-revisable by empirical anomalies; mathematics is a paradigm against which experience is judged
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical propositions are non-revisable in light of empirical investigation; anomalies in empirical demonstrations indicate bad exemplars, not falsity of mathematical identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat empirical failures as evidence of inadequacy of the experimental context rather than as refutations of mathematical truths; maintain the role of mathematics as measurement paradigm, not object measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wittgenstein is neither (simply) logicist, formalist, nor constructivist
rubrics_metrics.description: Wittgenstein's views do not neatly fit traditional 'isms' — he rejects logicism's epistemic reductionism, resists formalism's disembodied symbol-manipulation account, and does not accept intuitionist separations of mathematics from language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid categorizing Wittgenstein uncritically under standard labels; evaluate claims about his position by testing them against his insistence on language, practice, and the non-propositional status of mathematical formulae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of language-game and game analogies as diagnostic/argumentative method
rubrics_metrics.description: Wittgenstein frequently uses comparisons (e.g., 'What is chess about?') and language-game examples to dissolve philosophical confusions by showing how concepts function within specific practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ analogous practice-based examples to reveal misleading presuppositions: show how asking 'what is X about?' can import the wrong framework and produce pseudo-problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of mentalism/supermechanisms as explanations of rule-following
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject accounts that posit an inner 'guide' or 'supermechanism' in the mind that determines how rules are followed; such proposals lead to absurdities and are philosophically misguided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage explanatory moves that appeal to hidden cognitive mechanisms as regress-stoppers; instead describe the observable practices and the communal criteria that sustain rule-following.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophical diagnosis: distinguish philosophical from empirical questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some questions (e.g., 'Why do we all act the same way?') are empirical and demand scientific explanation; philosophers should not conflate these with conceptual confusions or attempt to answer empirical questions philosophically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When confronted with a philosophical puzzle, test whether it arises from a misuse of language (an illicit transfer) and resist turning it into an empirical research question unless appropriate; aim to describe, not to empirically explain, the background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational/pedagogical criterion: mastery through immersion and correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical understanding develops via immersion in a community, continual checking and correcting, and social pressures (e.g., grades); pedagogy inculcates the techniques enabling rule-recognition and right/wrong judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess mathematical competence by looking at training methods, communal correction mechanisms, and the degree to which learners acquire the 'technique' to treat certain regularities as normative.
